# Temple Scroll Column 34 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 34 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**34:1** The rooms on the west side of the outer court are for the Israelites who come up to worship Me at the temple.

**34:2** They shall bring their offerings, their sacrifices, their vow-offerings, and their voluntary gifts.

**34:3** There they shall eat — along with their sons and daughters, their male and female servants.

**34:4** No foreigner may eat any of the sacred food, for he has no right to it.

**34:5** The priests shall eat the most sacred offerings inside the inner court; the other sacred portions they shall eat in their assigned rooms in the outer court.

**34:6** Everyone shall eat in his own designated area; the groups must stay separate.

**34:7** Priests must not carry any sacred food out of their rooms into the outer court.

**34:8** They must not treat My sacred food carelessly — it is holy and must be handled as holy.

**34:9** When any Israelite brings a sacrifice, he shall go to whichever gate is closest to him.

**34:10** The Levites shall take it from him at the gate and deliver it to the priests at the altar.

**34:11** Each person shall bring his offering through the gate assigned to his own tribe.

**34:12** No one may use the gate belonging to another tribe — every tribe has its own entrance.

**34:13** The Levites shall be stationed at the gates to receive the offerings from the Israelites.

**34:14** They shall carry them to the altar and the storage rooms, placing each offering where it belongs.

**34:15** No one shall come into the outer court empty-handed during the festivals.

**34:16** Each person shall give what he can afford — in proportion to how the LORD his God has blessed him.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column details how offerings flow from worshipers through Levites to priests, with strict tribal gate assignments. The closing verse echoes Deuteronomy 16:17. The prohibition on crossing tribal gates is unique to the Temple Scroll and enforces a rigid social-spatial order.*
